question: How does the SP-C11-resorc[4]arene stationary phase perform in separating stereoisomers of combretastatins, and what factors influence its selectivity?
answer: The SP-C11-resorc[4]arene stationary phase effectively separates E/Z stereoisomers of combretastatins with high diastereoselectivity (α = 1.30–1.67) under reversed-phase HPLC conditions. The bowl-shaped cone stereoisomer immobilized on silica gel preferentially retains the (E)-isomer through stronger interactions, eluting the biologically active (Z)-isomer faster. Selectivity arises from the polar-embedded ester functionality and CH-π interactions with the resorc[4]arene cavity, while the C11-alkyl chains contribute to hydrophobic retention. The phase also exhibits versatility in separating polar small molecules and fullerenes through mixed-mode interactions.

The paper focuses on synthesizing and characterizing C-alkylated resorc[4]arenes with long C11 side chains and immobilizing them on a solid support to develop a polar-embedded stationary phase (SP-C11-resorc[4]arene). The stationary phase is evaluated for its ability to discriminate stereoisomers (E/Z combretastatins) and separate polar natural products (e.g., flavonoids) and fullerenes under different chromatographic conditions. Additionally, the study explores the self-assembly behavior of the chair stereoisomer in the crystal lattice via X-ray diffraction analysis, revealing unique halogen bonding interactions.
